newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy Senate commission delays telecom bill - source.
newsitem.headline: Italy Senate commission delays telecom bill - source.

text.p: The Public Works commission of the Italian Senate (upper house) has indefinitely postponed examination of a bill to set up a telecoms watchdog in response to filibustering, parliamentary sources said on Tuesday.

The commission was due to have begun examining some 400 amendments and 6,000 sub-amendments to the draft bill on Tuesday. The sources said the commission had abandoned work and no new date had been set.
The watchdog must be set up before the privatisation of state-controlled telecoms holding company Stet, which is due to take place by March 31 next year.

Michele Lauria, Undersecretary at the Post and Telecommunications Ministry, said earlier that the watchdog bill would remain hamstrung by "fouls" committed by political parties unless there was wide-ranging political clarification.
But he added: "The privatisation of Stet nevertheless remains set for the first months of 1997."
Prime Minister Romano Prodi said last week he hoped the bill would be approved by parliament in coming weeks in order not to delay the Stet sell-off.
The government has called two confidence votes in the past week to ram through legislation snarled by opposition filibustering.

However commentators said it would be impossible to use the same tactics in the watchdog bill because many of the proposed amendments had come from government ally, the hard-left Communist Refoundation party, which is ideologically opposed to the Stet privatisation.
Prodi's centre-left coalition depends on Communist Refoundation for a majority in the lower Chamber of Deputies.
